feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/analytics depth. It reads professionally, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, culminating in leadership roles with increasing scope, budget/governance responsibility, and strong digital transformation credibility.  
- Good use of scale indicators and specifics (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, named tools like GA4, BigQuery, Drupal), which strengthens impact and trust.  
- Strong alignment between summary, competencies, experience, and technical skills; positioning is consistent and targeted.

1. Top improvements  
- Tighten repetition and structure: “digital strategy/workflows/governance” appears many times across the summary, competencies, skills, and roles. Consolidate overlapping sections (“Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”).  
- Improve writing consistency: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; use the serial comma consistently (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); standardize hyphenation (e.g., “front-end,” “organization-wide,” “member-facing”).  
- Fix minor style/format issues: “English (Native)” and “French (A2/Learning)” should match style (e.g., “Native” / “A2”); “Ranked among the top public universities…” adds little value; consider bullet formatting instead of long dash-heavy paragraphs for readability.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, one or two concrete signals of scale, and less overlap with the competencies section.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Lead with current senior positioning and mission-driven/public-sector relevance, e.g. “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience in advocacy and membership organizations.”
- Add one concrete scale marker from recent roles, such as leading a 10,000+ page Drupal migration or overseeing channels reaching tens of thousands of stakeholders.
- Trim generic phrases like “building the workflows and systems” and replace with tighter language such as “designing governance, editorial workflows, and digital systems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “stakeholder coordination” repeat heavily from Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content” is strong; keep it, but avoid repeating similar wording elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize higher-value, differentiating capabilities rather than broad phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms like “Multi-channel communication” with more senior, outcome-oriented language such as “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Align wording with recent experience and technical depth: “CMS modernization,” “Editorial governance & workflow design,” and “Analytics, reporting & optimization.”
- Reduce soft-skill phrasing like “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” in favor of sharper competency language such as “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Cross-channel communications leadership • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial governance & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow architecture & content systems • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats several ideas already covered in the header and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, advocacy communication, analytics, and multimedia.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also overlaps with Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the opening, foreground the highest-impact work, and add outcomes or scale where possible.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opener with a sharper summary: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization in a full-time freelance engagement.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with verbs like “Led,” “Built,” “Developed,” “Advised.”
- Add measurable context where possible: size of web properties, number of stakeholders/publishers, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search improvement metrics, workflow time saved.
- Suggested phrasing:
- Led enterprise web and communications improvements across Drupal, analytics, and cross-channel content operations.
- Built campaign microsites, modular storytelling components, and member-facing toolkits within Drupal.
- Improved digital workflows, governance, and reporting to support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content, and user discovery experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance,” “analytics,” and “organization-wide communications” overlap with the 2022–2024 NACo role; keep this entry focused on new consulting impact and AI/search work.
- The microsite and AI search bullets duplicate Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same detail verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening emphasized enterprise ownership and if channel-management bullets added clearer outcomes rather than audience size alone.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + leadership: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management for a high-volume public-sector organization.”
- Tighten and front-load the biggest win: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Rephrase channel bullet to show business value: add engagement, growth, campaign support, or advocacy outcomes if available; otherwise shorten to avoid a generic “reaching thousands” statement.
- Combine infrastructure/operations into one impact bullet: “Built NACo’s analytics and publishing infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, strengthening reporting, governance, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video studio/buildout overlaps with older NACo video bullets; keep this focused on scaling in-house production capacity, not recurring video production.
- Governance/editorial coordination also appears in prior NACo roles; frame this here as enterprise-level systems leadership.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel growth, and systems/process improvements before the broader strategic remit of 2022–2024.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite opening to sharpen scope and progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector audience.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders” and “Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add measurable impact where possible: open/click rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, stakeholder groups supported, or workflow efficiencies.
- Replace softer phrasing like “helped improve” with ownership language: “Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, coordination and execution across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial coordination,” “publishing workflows,” and “video updates” also appear in adjacent NACo roles; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Leave website scale, governance, analytics, and studio-building to the Director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level leadership strengths and differentiate it from the technical and analytics skill groups.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more distinctive, outcome-oriented phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance, publishing operations & content systems
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience strategy, content planning & stakeholder alignment
- Consider changing “messaging” to “communications” to sound more senior and less tactical.
- Add one sharper leadership term like “transformation,” “operations,” or “stakeholder alignment” to reflect recent director/consulting work.
- Keep each line parallel in structure; avoid mixing broad functions with narrow tactics.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” overlap heavily with Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” also repeats the header summary; revise to add “membership” or “stakeholder” context instead.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities tied to modernization and delivery rather than listing every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery” instead of just “Drupal.”
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths: Drupal, CMS modernization, API integrations, workflow automation, AI-enabled search, front-end implementation.
- Remove lower-signal or older items unless central to target roles; consider dropping jQuery and possibly WordPress/SharePoint if not core to recent work.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations • Workflow automation and Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section duplicates the Technical + IT section; keep Topline Skills broader and reserve full tool lists for Technical + IT.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; keep only if it’s a signature differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” As a topline skills item, it should emphasize higher-value capabilities and outcomes over repeating software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.:
- Analytics strategy and reporting infrastructure
- GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity
- KPI framework design and executive reporting
- SEO, user behavior analysis, and performance optimization
- Put the business value first: “executive reporting” is stronger than “leadership reporting.”
- Group tools together on one line and reduce list fragmentation for cleaner scanning.
- If you can support it elsewhere, tie this area to impact such as “decision-making,” “content optimization,” or “channel performance improvement.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.
- It also overlaps with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep this section strategic, and leave the full tool list there.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets. Make it more senior, distinctive, and tied to delivery capability rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for scope and leadership: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio buildout and operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event technical direction”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to better match Director-level experience.
- Consider swapping “Hybrid and virtual event production” for “Livestream and hybrid event delivery” to sound more outcome-focused and less repetitive.
- If space allows elsewhere, move tool-level detail like PTZ to Technical + IT and keep this section focused on capabilities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies.
- “Studio operations” and video/livestream work are already evidenced in NACo experience; avoid repeating the same wording.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Use this item to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, rather than repeating the same tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Put Drupal first and add brief qualifiers only where you have recent, credible experience; this makes the list feel more senior and aligned to the work history.
- Standardize naming: use “Microsoft Power Pages” instead of “Power Pages” for clarity and ATS matching.
- If space allows, consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a notable project; it reads lighter than the rest.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section almost exactly.
- Avoid adding “CMS modernization” here since that already appears in Topline Skills and is better shown through the NACo migration bullet.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and slightly more current/senior.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize applied capability: “Front-End Development & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Integrations.”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- If accurate, add scope/impact via parenthetical qualifiers instead of more tools, e.g. “API integrations (CMS, analytics, campaign tools)” or “GitHub Actions (deployment/workflow automation).”
- Consider dropping version numbers unless matched elsewhere; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner and more senior.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “GitHub Actions” may fit better under “Automation & Workflow Systems” unless you specifically used it for deployment/technical implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Workflow automation / Airtable systems” in Topline Skills. Make it more selective and category-led so it supports recent systems leadership rather than listing every collaboration app used.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems
- Group by function for clarity: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams
- Consider trimming to the strongest/recent tools only, especially those tied to workflow design and automation leadership.
- If accurate, add a qualifier elsewhere, not here, such as “built workflow automation and cross-team planning systems” in recent roles rather than trying to show impact in this list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Slack and Teams are generic collaboration tools; they add less value than Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier.
- This item partially duplicates Topline Skills (“Workflow automation,” “Airtable systems”); avoid repeating the same emphasis verbatim.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to signal depth. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should stay tool-focused and, if possible, reflect enterprise-level use rather than repeat channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for readability: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope qualifier to show level of use: enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, member engagement
- Example rewrite: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • Enterprise email automation • Newsletter and member engagement operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “audience growth,” or “digital communications leadership” here; those are already covered in the 2022–2024 and 2018–2022 NACo roles.
- If Dynamics 365 was only limited exposure, keep it as-is without adding automation/strategy qualifiers.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Tighten it to emphasize foundational contributions, team-building, and any concrete scale or output.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving coordination across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add measurable scope if available: website refresh size, number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email volume, or workflow/time savings.
- Clarify your direct contribution: “supported” and “contributed” are weak; use “helped launch,” “produced,” “streamlined,” or “supervised.”
- Suggested version: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day supervision to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow language already used in later NACo roles unless you can specify a unique early-stage contribution.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or “firsts,” while avoiding overlap with later multimedia/digital leadership roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize initiative and scope: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the standout achievement the second clause: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, production coordination and rollout.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a clearer contribution such as “supported digital and multimedia content for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this item focused on innovation/research support plus the podcast first.
- Avoid overstating leadership here since stronger management/ownership appears in more recent NACo roles.
